transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just keep messing up little things. It's getting a bit frustrating. Like, I'll write down the completely wrong time on a class sheet over at the senior center. Or I'll be working on a project, measure a board, and still end up cutting it a hair short because I just sort of skipped over the small print on the plans. It's just straightforward, careless mistakes like that, and I figured I should come in and talk to somebody about it.
Have you noticed these kinds of careless mistakes and attention slips your whole life, even back in school, or is this something that's really only started recently?

No, it's definitely not a new thing. It's been happening my whole life, really. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, but... well, I was always forgetting my books or losing my homework. They'd say I would just sit there staring out the window unless somebody was right there to keep me on track. So, yeah, it goes way back.
Besides these attention slips, do you often feel restless, fidgety, or find yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting things out—in your daily life?

Well, I don't really do the blurting things out or interrupting people so much. But as for feeling restless... yeah, I definitely get that. 

If I'm trying to sit through a whole meeting, or, you know, even just having a quiet evening at the condo, I get this sort of ants-in-my-pants feeling. I just want to get up, check on something, or putter around a bit. It's just hard for me to sit completely still for very long.
Thinking back to your childhood and teenage years, did you also experience that same restless, 'ants-in-your-pants' feeling, or is that something that's developed more recently in adulthood?

No, I don't really remember feeling like that back then. I mean, I was always a bit distracted, like I said, but I don't recall being particularly fidgety or restless as a kid or a teenager. That sort of physical restlessness, where I just can't sit still, feels like something that's crept up on me more as an adult.

Would you say these attention slips and forgetfulness cause real problems for you in more than one area of your life—like at work, at home, and in your social activities—or is it mostly limited to just one setting?

Yeah, it definitely spills over into a few different areas. It's not just one thing. Like, I used to help lead a couple of DIY workshops down at the community center, but... well, the mix-ups just got to be too much, so I had to step back from that. And at home, my wife has started double-checking all our plans. If she doesn't, I end up throwing off the schedule for family visits or, you know, other activities we have going on. So, yeah, it definitely causes issues in more than one place.
I'm sorry, did you ask me something else just now? I think my mind just wandered for a second and I completely missed it.
Aside from the restlessness you mentioned as an adult, can you recall if, as a child, you were often described as 'always on the go,' talked excessively, or had trouble staying seated in class?

No, I don't think so. I wasn't really a hyper kid. I mean, I didn't get in trouble for running around or talking too much in class or anything like that. I was more the type to just sit there and daydream, to be honest. So, no, I wouldn't say I was always on the go back then.

Besides feeling restless, do you currently find yourself talking more than others think is necessary, feeling uncomfortable being quiet during activities, or feeling driven to keep busy as if you can't relax?

Well, I wouldn't say I talk excessively or anything like that. But... I do have a hard time just being quiet when I'm supposed to be relaxing. Like, if I try to sit quietly and read, or if I'm at one of those calm group activities down at the center, I just can't seem to settle. Before long, I'm tapping my foot, or clearing my throat, or just making little comments to myself. I don't mean to bother anyone, it's just... hard to just sit still and be quiet.
Have you noticed this restlessness being linked to periods of worry, stress, or low mood, or does it happen even when you're feeling completely calm and content?

I wouldn't say it's linked to worry or feeling down. It's just... there. Even when I'm having a good day and I'm not stressed about anything, I still get that feeling like I can't just sit and relax. It doesn't seem to matter what kind of mood I'm in.
